newsitem.title: USA: Continental Air, pilots far apart on labor pact.
newsitem.headline: Continental Air, pilots far apart on labor pact.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc and its pilots union, which have been in labor negotiations since April, remain far apart on key economic issues but are optimistic on reaching an agreement by October.
The two sides sparred Wednesday, with the pilots union taking aim at Continental's better-than-expected second quarter results and its improving cash position.
On economic issues, "We're probably about as far apart as Tokyo is to Paris," Continental Airlines Chairman Gordon Bethune.
But "We have done an amazing amount of issues resolution in the last couple of months" on other areas of the contract, Bethune said.
Continental has previously said it is amenable to wage increases, but the extent of those increases is in debate.
The pilots union contends its members earn about 40 percent less than industry average wages. The pilots union said it now wants pay comparable to its peers at the nation's largest airlines.
"We're not going to settle a contract that dosen't put our pilot group on par with the big five airlines with respect to pay, retirement" and other benefits, the union said Wednesday.
Continental said the pilots' contract demands would add about $430 million a year in costs over the current $400 million annual pilot payroll budget.
The pilots union called the company's counter proposal, which offered wage increases of about 36 percent over several years, "woefully inadequate."

"The company continues to spend money buying airplanes, making acquisitions and retiring but continues to refuse to spend money on its most precious asset, its employees," said Bill Borrelli, vice president of the Independent Association of Continental Pilots. "The company continues to improve its cash position while continuing to maintain a tight-fisted bargaining position," Borrelli said.

Continental's second quarter earnings dropped to $1.64 per diluted share from $2.04 per diluted share a year ago, but exceeded Wall Street expectations. Second quarter revenues increased to $1.79 billion from $1.64 billion.
The airline's cash balance of $994 million, up from $825 million last year.
Talks between the two sides are in recess and will resume after August 5.
